title: Pricing futures: cost of carry and basis
body_md:
## Cost of carry

**Fair futures price F = S × (1 + r × t)** (simple) or **S × e^(r t)** (continuous), less the present value of any **dividends** expected before expiry.

Example: S = 100, r = 8% a year, t = 3 months: F = 100 × (1 + 0.08 × 0.25) = **102**.

## Basis

**Basis = spot − futures** (some texts use futures − spot; read the question). Basis **converges to zero** at expiry.

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Contango** | Futures above spot (normal, cost of carry positive) |
| **Backwardation** | Futures below spot |

## Cash-and-carry arbitrage

If the futures price is **above** fair value: buy spot, sell futures, hold to expiry, pocket the difference. If **below**: reverse (sell spot, buy futures).

## Factors

Interest rates, dividends, time to expiry, demand for hedging.

> **Exam tip:** Dividends reduce fair futures price; higher interest raises it.
example: Spot 200, r = 6%, t = 6 months, no dividends: F = 200 × (1 + 0.06 × 0.5) = 206. If the market price is 210, buy spot, sell the future and lock in 4.
say: The futures price reflects financing cost, not a forecast.
At expiry, the future and spot converge.
never: Futures predict where the price will be.
